finding.title: Counter classifier omits the existing durable-encoding batch map
finding.violatedRelation: The measurement claims total source attribution for event-reference Map operations, but declares only two non-ordinal live-map categories while the measured owner path performs three such maps' inserts. Unknown-operation zero is the correct guard; the category population is incomplete.
finding.cause: Map.prototype.get and Map.prototype.set both increment the same unattributed bucket. The set wrapper classifies live numeric entries during appendValidated separately, then assigns the first two other map identities to stagedBodyEntries/stagedEventEntries. Every further identity goes to unattributed. appendDurablyBatch creates a separate batchEvents map and sets each already-admitted event once while encoding the transaction.
causalChain: The test measures the entire admitRuntimeEventTransaction, including the final durable commit, for a chain of N workspace public_operation_admitted events with E=N-1 causes.

Inside the transaction, admitRuntimeEventInternal skips immediate durable append and calls stageRuntimeEvent. Admission validates each causal ref through RuntimeHistorySelection.rowById; RuntimeHistory.appendValidated separately checks its causal location and inserts its event-id ordinal.
stageRuntimeEvent then inserts into runtimeHistoryStagedBodies and state.eventsById. These are the first two non-ordinal event-reference Map identities captured by the classifier.

After the callback returns, the transaction calls appendDurablyBatch. Its local batchEvents map retains this batch's earlier events for existing body-encoding references, with committed-row fallback constrained to the committed prefix.
Each event is encoded before batchEvents.set(event.eventId,event). This adds exactly N sets to the third non-ordinal live map and preserves earlier-only lookup semantics.

The classifier maps that third identity to unattributed. For N=128, the predicted128 entries equal the entire observed unattributed total. All counter contributions are nonnegative, so no additional unknown gets/sets are needed to explain that observed total.
